channel.title: Nolan Kido Poker
channel.description: Poker episodes, hand reviews, stories, and reading guides.

item.title: From the first seat to the end of the day.
item.description: Prepare for breaks, table moves, bagging chips and finishing a tournament day without treating each logistical step as a strategic problem.

item.title: Plan the day. Keep the hand. Check the source.
item.description: Three printable, copyable and downloadable private-use sheets for event planning, completed-hand capture and evaluating a poker resource.

item.title: Registration, re-entry and the cost of another attempt.
item.description: Separate advance registration, starting flights, re-entry and rebuys, then account for each payment without treating previous losses as a reason to continue.

item.title: Keep a hand note you can actually review.
item.description: Capture positions, stacks, actions and uncertainty after play, with a checked fictional pot ledger and a reusable private note template.

item.title: The live tournament field guide.
item.description: Seven practical guides for choosing an event, preparing for tournament day, recording completed hands and evaluating study resources.

item.title: Your first live tournament, without the guesswork.
item.description: Prepare for registration, finding your seat, asking procedural questions, and leaving with one useful observation.

item.title: Read poker advice without borrowing its certainty.
item.description: Evaluate a video, chart, article or forum answer by its question, evidence and assumptions, then turn it into one checkable study task.

item.title: Choose a study tool by the question it answers.
item.description: Distinguish equity calculators, ICM calculators, solvers, solution libraries and trainers before spending money or interpreting a result.

item.title: Read the structure before choosing the tournament.
item.description: Compare total cost, starting big blinds, blind progression and time commitments using two fictional event structures.

item.title: Results deserve context.
item.description: Separate tournament ROI, trip costs, sample uncertainty and decision evidence with worked accounting and probability examples.

item.title: When more chips are not enough.
item.description: A checkable three-player ICM example explains prize equity, risk premiums and why gaining chips can lower expected payout.

item.title: Three all-ins. Two pots.
item.description: Separate a fictional three-way all-in into a main pot, side pot and refund, then check the winners and final stacks.

item.title: A short stack is a situation, not a chart.
item.description: Record stacks, antes, action trees and tournament objectives before comparing short-stack decisions or push/fold references.

item.title: From possible hands to weighted ranges.
item.description: Count physical combinations, remove known cards, weight betting frequencies and test a fictional river range.

item.title: Twelve checks. One useful repair.
item.description: Twelve answer-reveal exercises on pot odds, ranges, short stacks, ICM, results and honest poker storytelling.

item.title: Pot odds, with the assumptions visible.
item.description: Price calls and raises, distinguish draw probabilities from equity, and test the assumptions behind a bluff or call.

item.title: From hand notes to a poker vlog.
item.description: An editing workbench for honest hand reconstruction, clear graphics, useful narration and poker episode companion pages.

item.title: The flush arrives. What can still change?
item.description: Follow a fictional flush through the turn and river, count all remaining cards, and distinguish improving from winning.

item.title: One river. Two different stories.
item.description: A visual, fictional river exercise: price a call, test the assumed range and reveal two endings without confusing the result with the decision.

item.title: Questions new viewers ask.
item.description: Read the player, action, pot, and call amount in a poker graphic. Find a specific hand or companion and keep later commentary separate from the record.

item.title: How a tournament unfolds.
item.description: Understand the changing blinds, the money bubble, re-entries, and the difference between a large chip stack and a cash result.

item.title: Which kind of tournament is this?
item.description: Decode fixed, progressive and mystery bounties, equal-seat satellites and structure sheets so that the same chips do not imply the same prize.

item.title: What is happening at the table?
item.description: Understand floor calls, chip declarations, the clock and spectator boundaries without judging an entire live hand from a short edited clip.

item.title: Follow the action.
item.description: Follow your first poker hand without reading a full course. Find the player, the action, the amount to call, and a direct explanation when needed.

item.title: What changed on the board?
item.description: Read suits, connected cards, paired boards and draws. See why one new community card can change the meaning of the same hole cards.

item.title: What is the bet trying to do?
item.description: Understand ranges, combinations, blockers, value bets and bluffs without treating a commentator’s guess as knowledge of hidden cards.

item.title: Why does the seat matter?
item.description: Follow position, heads-up action order, effective stacks and stack-to-pot ratio without mistaking a seat label for a strategy.

item.title: What the percentages mean.
item.description: Separate the price of a call, the chance of completing a draw, and the uncertainty in a hand review. They are not interchangeable numbers.

item.title: One hand, from deal to showdown.
item.description: Follow a complete hand, learn who acts when, and see why winning the pot is different from winning the same amount in profit.

item.title: Review a hand, not just the result.
item.description: A practical method for reviewing a tournament poker decision, with a worked fictional hand, clear uncertainty labels, and a blank review sheet.

item.title: Which hand wins?
item.description: A visual reference to the ten familiar hand labels, followed by the kicker, shared-board, and ace-low situations that often confuse new viewers.

item.title: Poker terms, in plain language.
item.description: Forty-eight short entries grouped by what you are trying to understand. Use the topic links, or your browser’s Find command, to look up a word without reading everything.

item.title: Pause the hand. Read the situation.
item.description: Work through three fictional scenes: calling a raise, a winner that changes twice, and a river decision where price is not the same as equity.

item.title: Bets, calls, and side pots.
item.description: Read the amount a player actually adds, understand why a short stack can still win, and keep the pot separate from the size of a wager.
